reason: E2 directly supports nanoclustering-induced GB embrittlement and the role of Cr, Ni, Mn segregation in ductility loss at intermediate temperatures in CrMnFeCoNi HEAs. E4 supports the mitigating effect of preexisting Cr-rich precipitates. However, E1 concerns a different alloy system (TiVNbTa) and impurity-driven softening, not principal-element nanosegregation, and E3 discusses grain-size effects and intermetallic formation rather than the specific nanocluster decohesion mechanism. The role of chemical short-range order is not directly evidenced in the cited passages.
premises: Principal elements in single-phase HEAs can segregate to grain boundaries at intermediate temperatures
This segregation forms nanoclusters that reduce grain-boundary cohesion
Reduced cohesion causes a transition from ductile transgranular to brittle intergranular fracture
Chemical short-range order facilitates the segregation and nanoclustering
Preexisting Cr-rich precipitates can absorb embrittling elements and mitigate ductility loss
